indication_area: Complicated bacterial infections (intra-abdominal, skin, pneumonia, UTI, pelvic) and surgical prophylaxis

approval_evidence.quote: 11/21/2001 ORIG-1 Approval Type 1 - New Molecular Entity (NDA 021337, INVANZ ERTAPENEM SODIUM)

series_start_reason: The series starts at 2002Q1, the first quarter for which the legacy Merck filings searched (CIK 64978) print an Invanz sales figure. The FDA cleared Invanz in November 2001 (launch_evidence); no figure for the rest of 2001 appears in those filings.

launch_evidence.quote: In November 2001, the FDA cleared Invanz (ertapenem sodium), a new once-a-day injectable antibiotic, for marketing in the United States for the treatment of adults with the following moderate to severe infections caused by susceptible strains of the designated organisms: complicated intra-abdominal infections, complicated skin and skin structure infections

series_end_reason: Merck's Table 3a prints an INVANZ row through the fourth-quarter 2022 release (8-K filed 2023-02-02); the first-quarter 2023 release (filed 2023-04-27, Ex. 99.1 and 99.2) and later releases contain no INVANZ text.
search_log: Listed every filing of CIK 64978 (legacy Merck & Co., Inc., now Merck Sharp & Dohme LLC) 2000-2010 and CIK 310158 (Schering-Plough, renamed Merck & Co., Inc. in November 2009) 2000-2026, all forms; fetched every 10-Q/10-K main document and every htm/txt document of every 8-K/8-K/A with earnings items (2.02, 12, 7/9).

2002Q1-2009Q3 from the legacy Merck quarterly 'worldwide sales of selected products' schedule (Global amount; 2002 amounts are printed rounded to $5 million); 2009Q4 from the supplemental combined non-GAAP table of Merck's 4Q 2009 release (a full three months); 2010Q1-2022Q4 from Table 3a, Global current quarter. Quarter checked against each release's header.
